panels.title: Multi-platform build with registry cache
panels.body:
# Create a multi-platform builder
docker buildx create --name multi --driver docker-container --use

# Build for amd64 + arm64, push to registry
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --cache-from type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:cache \
  --cache-to   type=registry,ref=ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:cache,mode=max \
  --attest type=sbom \
  --attest type=provenance,mode=max \
  -t ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:v1.2.3 \
  --push .

# GitHub Actions cache backend (no registry needed)
docker buildx build \
  --cache-from type=gha \
  --cache-to   type=gha,mode=max \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  -t myapp:latest --push .

panels.title: Critical buildx gotchas
panels.body:
--load and multi-platform are mutually exclusive.
--load writes to the local Docker image store, which can only hold
one platform. Use --push for multi-arch, or build single-platform
locally and use --load for that.

cache-to mode=max vs mode=min:
  max: caches ALL intermediate layers (every RUN, COPY). Best cache-hit
       rate but larger cache storage.
  min: caches only the final image layers. Smaller but fewer hits.

Builders are not shared between contexts. 'docker buildx ls' shows
builders per context. CI jobs each create their own unless you
explicitly configure a remote buildkitd.

The default 'docker' driver does NOT support --push or --platform
with multiple values — you must create a 'docker-container' driver.

panels.title: Cache backend selection
pros: type=gha: zero extra infra — works in GitHub Actions; survives across jobs within a workflow
type=registry: portable across any CI system; shares cache between branches via tag naming
cons: type=gha: limited to GitHub Actions; 10 GB cap per repo; purged after 7 days of inactivity
type=registry: requires a registry write credential; adds push/pull overhead on every build
